person.name: Behzad Mahdavi
person.text: Executive Chairman of Biodextris and its Chief Commercial Officer, leading global commercial expansion (appointed June 2025). 25+ years in CDMO and CRO services: about **13 years at Lonza** in leadership roles, then **VP of Global Open Innovation at Catalent**, then **SVP Biopharma Manufacturing & Life Science Tools at Ginkgo Bioworks** (from 2022). Earlier CEO of SAM Electron Technologies. Executive Chairman of **OpenCell Technologies** (Missouri; non-viral cell transfection) since Oct 2023. PhD in chemistry (Université de Sherbrooke), MBA (UQAM). Speaker at SynBioBeta 2025.

company.text: Biodextris is a contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) in Laval, Québec, built on GSK's former biologics and vaccine development operations. It covers process development, analytics, QC and GMP manufacturing for biologics, vaccines, and cell and gene therapies, from early research to clinical and commercial supply. Its Laval Biotech City centre (C$25M fit-out, opened 2023) has five cGMP suites and 50–200 L bioreactors. Clean Biologics, backed by healthcare investor **ArchiMed**, bought it in May 2021. On **Sep 29, 2026** it named **Clement Fourny** CEO (ex-SVP Commercial, SmartLabs Boston; earlier Cytiva).

talking_points: Following our June 9 call — what has changed since, especially with Clement Fourny joining as CEO?
What is your role now — still Executive Chairman and CCO at Biodextris, and what is innov2gro?
Which of your biotech clients or portfolio companies work on rare disease or hereditary cancer, where DNA + RNA data could sharpen patient selection?
Do your cell and gene therapy clients ask for genomic or transcriptomic analysis alongside manufacturing?
As an advisor to start-ups: what would you tell a European diagnostics company entering the US market this year?
